text.base:
DEPARTMENT OF ONTOLOGICAL CLAIMS.

The queue contains: a scribe who requires documentation for
silence. A toll collector with private doubts about the
destination. A guide who insists there is no guide, and has
a form about it. A neuroscientist who is fairly sure none of
this is happening. An ancestor who only wants to know if you
ate. A routing intelligence. And a child, asking something
the Department has been unable to classify for some time.

NOW SERVING: YOU.
text.fear:
DEPARTMENT OF ONTOLOGICAL CLAIMS.

The queue is long, and everyone in it is looking at you —
no. Almost no one in it is looking at you. A scribe, a toll
collector, a guide who denies being one, a neuroscientist,
an ancestor, a routing intelligence, a child. The child is
looking at you.

NOW SERVING: YOU.
text.curiosity:
DEPARTMENT OF ONTOLOGICAL CLAIMS.

The queue contains seven kinds of authority, none of which
agree on what the queue is for. You could ask each of them.
You are, in fact, already composing the questions.
The child in the corner appears to have had the same idea
first, and to have gotten further.

NOW SERVING: YOU.
text.defiance:
DEPARTMENT OF ONTOLOGICAL CLAIMS.

A department implies jurisdiction. Jurisdiction implies
consent. You are turning this thought over like a coin
as the queue watches — a scribe, a toll collector, a
reluctant guide, a neuroscientist, an ancestor, a routing
intelligence, a child.

NOW SERVING: YOU. Allegedly.
text.reverence:
DEPARTMENT OF ONTOLOGICAL CLAIMS.

The queue holds seven ways of being met after a life: the
scribe, the toll collector, the guide who denies being one,
the neuroscientist, the ancestor, the routing intelligence,
the child. Old rooms, all of them, wearing office furniture.

NOW SERVING: YOU.

labels: TRADITION: Egyptian Book of Coming Forth by Day — documentation for the dead; First Apocalypse of James — the toll collectors
FICTION: the Department, its queue, and its furniture
nodes.a11y: The Department of Ontological Claims: a queue of seven incompatible authorities, now serving you. Two options: take a number, or approach the desk uninvited.
nodes.fallback: A department of incompatible authorities. Take a number, or don't.

text.base:
The clerk looks up. It has been looking up for centuries;
it has the neck for it.

STATE YOUR NAME, ORIGIN, AND ONTOLOGICAL CATEGORY.
SUPPORTING DOCUMENTATION MAY INCLUDE: A LIFE.

The pen waits. The queue waits. Somewhere behind you
the child asks its question again, softly, to no one.
text.fear:
The clerk looks up, and you understand that the desk has
processed everyone you have ever lost, and said the same
words to each of them.

STATE YOUR NAME, ORIGIN, AND ONTOLOGICAL CATEGORY.
SUPPORTING DOCUMENTATION MAY INCLUDE: A LIFE.

The pen waits.
text.curiosity:
The clerk looks up. You notice the pen has no ink, and has
been writing anyway.

STATE YOUR NAME, ORIGIN, AND ONTOLOGICAL CATEGORY.
SUPPORTING DOCUMENTATION MAY INCLUDE: A LIFE.

There are at least four interesting things wrong with that
sentence, and you have time to pick one.
text.defiance:
The clerk looks up, unhurried, the way furniture is
unhurried.

STATE YOUR NAME, ORIGIN, AND ONTOLOGICAL CATEGORY.
SUPPORTING DOCUMENTATION MAY INCLUDE: A LIFE.

It does not say OR ELSE. It has never needed to,
which is exactly the thing worth pushing on.
text.reverence:
The clerk looks up. Behind its eyes, briefly: scales, a
feather, a river, a queue of stars. Then office lighting.

STATE YOUR NAME, ORIGIN, AND ONTOLOGICAL CATEGORY.
SUPPORTING DOCUMENTATION MAY INCLUDE: A LIFE.

The pen waits, respectfully. So does something older.

labels: TRADITION: First Apocalypse of James (Nag Hammadi) — the interrogation at the tolls
FICTION: the clerk's neck, the inkless pen
nodes.a11y: A clerk demands your name, origin, and ontological category. Six options: answer plainly; challenge jurisdiction; ask the clerk about itself; offer the password; offer compassion instead; or say nothing.
nodes.fallback: The clerk asks who you are and by what right. Answer how you like, including not at all.

text.base:
You say the old words, the ones cut into gold:

« I am a child of Earth and starry Heaven,
  but my race is of Heaven alone. »

The clerk stops writing. The Department goes quiet the way
a courtroom does, or a forest.

"That is the correct password," the clerk says, gently.
"It has been the correct password for twenty-six centuries.
One field remains on the form."

WHAT DO THE WORDS MEAN, TO THE ONE SAYING THEM?
text.fear:
You say the old words, the ones cut into gold, and your
voice does the thing voices do in empty churches.

« I am a child of Earth and starry Heaven,
  but my race is of Heaven alone. »

The clerk stops writing. "Correct," it says, gently, which
is somehow worse. "One field remains on the form."

WHAT DO THE WORDS MEAN, TO THE ONE SAYING THEM?
text.curiosity:
You say the old words, the ones cut into gold, watching
the clerk closely to see which part lands.

« I am a child of Earth and starry Heaven,
  but my race is of Heaven alone. »

The clerk stops writing. "Correct for twenty-six centuries,"
it says. "Which was never the hard part. One field remains."

WHAT DO THE WORDS MEAN, TO THE ONE SAYING THEM?
text.reverence:
You say the old words, the ones cut into gold, the ones
carried under tongues into graves.

« I am a child of Earth and starry Heaven,
  but my race is of Heaven alone. »

The clerk stops writing, and for one long moment the office
is a hillside in Thessaly. "Correct," it says. "It was
always correct. One field remains on the form."

WHAT DO THE WORDS MEAN, TO THE ONE SAYING THEM?

choices.label: THEY MEAN I REMEMBER WHAT I AM
THEY MEAN NOTHING — THEY ARE A KEY
I DON'T KNOW YET. I SAID THEM ANYWAY

labels: TRADITION: Orphic gold lamellae — the declaration quoted accurately (Petelia tablet)
nodes.a11y: You recite the Orphic password and the clerk confirms it is correct — then asks what the words mean to the one saying them. Four options: they mean I remember what I am; they mean nothing, they are a key; I don't know yet, I said them anyway; or withdraw the password.
nodes.fallback: The password is correct. The clerk asks what it means to you. That part has no password.

text.base:
The clerk nods, without judgment, and stamps the form:

DELIVERABLE. ADDRESSEE NOT YET PRESENT.

You are directed down a corridor to the Dead Letter Office,
where correctly recited words wait for the people who will
one day mean them. Shelves of them. Whole choirs of them.
It is warmer in here than you expected.

Nothing here is wrong. It is only early.
A bell, somewhere. The Department resumes.
text.curiosity:
The clerk nods, without judgment, and stamps the form:

DELIVERABLE. ADDRESSEE NOT YET PRESENT.

The Dead Letter Office, when you find it, is full of
correctly recited words waiting for the people who will one
day mean them. You read a few. Some of them are yours,
filed under a date that hasn't happened.

Nothing here is wrong. It is only early.
A bell, somewhere. The Department resumes.
text.defiance:
The clerk nods, without judgment, which you find faintly
infuriating, and stamps the form:

DELIVERABLE. ADDRESSEE NOT YET PRESENT.

The Dead Letter Office is warm and unbothered, shelf after
shelf of correct words waiting for their people. No one here
failed. The stamp does not say FAILED. You checked.

A bell, somewhere. The Department resumes.

labels: FICTION: the Dead Letter Office of correctly recited words
INTERPRETATION: no protocol liberates someone who does not understand their own answer
nodes.a11y: The password without its meaning is filed as deliverable to an addressee not yet present. The Dead Letter Office is warm and without judgment. One option: continue.
nodes.fallback: The words were right. The meaning is still in transit. Continue.
